What is the difference between paging and segmentation?

Paging divides memory into fixed-size blocks called pages, which are mapped to physical memory frames. Segmentation divides memory into variable-size blocks called segments, which are based on logical units like functions or data structures. Paging is simpler and avoids external fragmentation, while segmentation provides better logical organization but can suffer from external fragmentation.

How can deadlock be prevented?

Deadlock is a situation in which a set of processes are blocked because each process is holding a resource and waiting for another resource acquired by some other process. Deadlock can be prevented by ensuring that at least one of the four necessary conditions (mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait) is not satisfied. How does load balancing work in a cluster?

In a cluster, load balancing works by distributing incoming network traffic across multiple servers. This is typically managed by a load balancer, which acts as a reverse proxy, receiving client requests and forwarding them to the appropriate server based on predefined algorithms. This ensures that no single server becomes a bottleneck, improving the overall performance and reliability of the system.
